title: Passing OffscreenCanvas (with its context) back to main thread (or another thread).
body:
I thought I could do something simple: send a canvas to a worker, draw on it, and finally send it back to main thread to use as a WebGL texture.

However, once an OffscreenCanvas has a context inside the worker, it can not be sent back, and results in this error:

```js
An OffscreenCanvas could not be cloned because it had a rendering context
```

To do what I want to do, I would have to have two canvas: one on main thread, one in the worker, then send an `ImageBitmap` or some other transferable from the worker to the main thread and put the data into the main thread canvas. This has a big downside: triple the memory usage.

Manipulating a 500MB bitmap equates to using 1.5 GB of memory: one canvas on the main thread (~500MB), one canvas in the worker (~500MB), and finally the transferable object that we pass between threads (500MB).

We could at least eliminate the 500MB of transferable memory if we were able to [write to the buffer of a canvas](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/6611)

---

## use case

I would like to manipulate 500MB of incoming PNG in a worker, without using more than 500MB of memory (after decode, and before WebGL GPU allocation).

It's not possible, unless I abandon using built-in APIs and do it myself in using a Transferable typed array or a SharedArrayBuffer along with custom decoder.

The smallest size possible with built-in APIs uses double the desired memory for manipulation:

- worker receives a PNG (I'm not including this memory, no way around it).
- draw it to canvas in a worker (makes 500MB)
- put the result in a tranferable or SAB (uses or re-uses 500MB, respectively)
- pass the mem to main thread and use it in a WebGL call (we're not counting the memory in the GPU, that is out of userland control)

There's no way to halve that (the userland memory allocation) that I know of, apart from abandoning built-in image processing APIs (canvas) and using our own image decoders, which defeats the purpose because now we have duplicate code (built into the browser, and into the web app).

## solution

Maybe we can expand the OffscreenCanvas API so that when it is transfered, its context will be deactivated in the worker, and calling `getContext()` on the receiving side would work as one would expect without throwing an error.

The context could be usable only in the thread where the offscreen canvas was passed to.

It seems that adding this functionality would be a mostly non-breaking change. The only code that would break is code that checks for those errors, which would no longer happen.

Ideally we would be able to do the following:

- main thread passes canvas to worker (main thread can not use the canvas now)
- worker receives a png and draws it to canvas, manipulates any pixels
- worker passes canvas back to main thread (worker can not use the canvas anymore, but now the main thread can)
- main thread passes the canvas element to a WebGL texture

The only memory that the user had to allocate manually was the 2d context with its width and height, and pass it (the canvas) around for manipulation and finally to WebGL where it is used as a texture.
